Full read: Tuesday's session, where it leaves the board, and what today decides

Tuesday sold the first hour, printed the low in the second and bought the afternoon. Eighteen of 25 fell, an average 0.9%, after Monday's 25 of 25; 23 first hours printed the day's high and 21 lows came in the 10:30 hour, with nine closes in the top 30% of the range. The deepest: IONQ −6.1%, HOOD −4.0%, ORCL −3.4%, IGV −3.3%, PLTR −2.4% and MSFT −2.3%; the best: SPCX +3.2%, AVGO +2.5% and MRVL +2.3%. SPY fell 1.0% to 732.44, its lowest close since Jul 29, 2.06 under its 200-day on 1.48× volume, a fourth straight lower close.

Where it leaves the board. The daily column reads 1 up, 6 mixed and 18 down, from 1 / 5 / 19: SPCX turned mixed from down. Three of the 20 single names close over their 10-day (AAPL, SPCX, AVGO), from one; two over their 21-day (AAPL, AVGO), from one; three over their 50-day (AAPL, AMZN, TSLA), from four, MSFT the loss; five over their 200-day (AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, TSLA, AMD), TSLA rejoining by 32 cents. The hourly column reads 2 up and 21 down, from 0 and 24; the 15m column turned mixed in sixteen names on the last hour's bounce and reads 2 up, 18 mixed, 5 down.

What today decides. Where NVDA opens against 165.17 and 148.80 with the report out and the feed pointing higher; the chip cards (AMD, AVGO, MU, MRVL, SNDK, SKHY, INTC) read off that bar before their own levels. Extension table: how far each name sits from its own mean

(Close − EMA21) ÷ ATR-14 on the daily frame. Beyond ±2 is stretched; beyond ±3 is a chart that has outrun anything able to catch it. Extension is not a timing signal: it is a position-size input and a map of how far an unwind travels before it finds structure.

BandNames (daily ext, ATR units)What it means today

Day-trading playbook

Wednesday opens on NVDA's event bar with the feed pointing higher, on an index that closed under its 200-day and on a Tuesday that printed its lows in the 10:30 hour and bought the afternoon, so the session is gap rules first and holds second: NVDA is read against 165.17 and 148.80 before anything else, the chip cards read off its bar, SPY is read against 734.50, AVGO and SPCX trade their second-close lines (335.85, 139.61), MSFT its avoid line (504.96), AAPL its 10-day (350.70), and the FOMC minutes at 14:00 are the afternoon's event.

Session framing

Tuesday put 23 of 25 first hours at the day's high and 21 lows in the 10:30 hour, then bought every hour after it in most names: nine closed in the top 30% of their range and the 15m cell turned mixed in sixteen. The long side of the board is one name over its 21-day, AAPL, and two names one close from cautious, AVGO and SPCX; MSFT, AMZN and TSLA hold their 50-day or sit near it, and everything else is an avoid card with a floor at Tuesday's afternoon low and an upgrade line overhead. Day trades live in that gap; stances move only on daily closes.

Four questions govern the session. Where NVDA opens against 165.17, one ATR over the close, and 148.80, the 52-week low, with the report out. Whether SPY gets back over 734.50, its 200-day, and whether QQQ holds 646.64, Tuesday's low. Whether the second closes come: AVGO over 335.85 and SPCX over 139.61 to cautious. And whether the last lines hold: MSFT 504.96, AAPL 350.70, AMZN 256.62, TSLA 376.69, AMD 497.80.

Methodology and data notes

Pipeline, rubric, data caveats and sources

Pipeline: TradingView Desktop (CDP) → dedicated "B List Research" layout → up to 500 bars per timeframe per symbol (W / D / 240 / 60 / 15, regular sessions) → indicators computed locally: EMA 10/21/50/200, RSI-14 (Wilder), MACD 12/26/9, ATR-14 (Wilder), 20-bar relative volume, fractal (2-2) swing pivots, 252-day high/low distances, relative strength vs SPY as return differentials. Trend matrix rubric per cell, ±1 for each of six inputs: close vs EMA21, close vs EMA50, EMA21/EMA50 stack, EMA50 five-bar slope, RSI zone (≥55 = +1, ≤45 = −1, else 0) and MACD histogram sign — score ≥+4 Up, ≤−4 Down, else Chop; cells lacking an EMA21 or EMA50 return "—".

Data caveats. Captured Wednesday Nov 18 2026 at 07:43 ET, before the open. No symbol errored and every frame of every symbol ends on Tuesday Nov 17's completed session: the daily on the Nov 17 bar, the 4H on the 13:30 bar, the 1H on the 15:30 bar and the 15m on the 15:45 bar; nothing was rebuilt or patched before the build. The weekly column is the Nov 16–20 running bar after two sessions, so the weekly badges are provisional (none changed on Tuesday) and are confirmed or reversed on Friday's close. The prior scan for every day-over-day comparison (change chips, breadth tile, census) is Tuesday morning's daily scan, which held Monday Nov 16's session. "Tuesday" in the cards is Nov 17, "Monday" Nov 16, "Friday" Nov 13 and "Thursday" Nov 12; Wednesday Nov 11 and earlier sessions carry their dates; today's session is "today" or "the open" and NVDA's is "the event bar". Every time in this report is Eastern standard time; hours are named by the time they open ("the first hour" is 09:30–10:30, "the last hour" 15:30–16:00). The 15m column is Tuesday's 15:45 ET bar. The final 15m bars carry the usual closing-auction volume spike and those RVOL figures were not used anywhere in this report; 15-minute readings quoted are RSI, extension and EMA position only. The same applies to 1H and 4H relative volume. All relative-volume figures in this report are daily. Hourly bars and the daily bar can differ at the open and the close (auction prints); closes and ranges are quoted from the daily bar and intraday paths from the hourly bars (NVDA's 158.19 daily high against a 157.46 first-hour high, SMH's 460.10 daily close against a 460.25 last hourly close, AMD 503.41 against 503.55, MU 712.42 against 712.98, AVGO 341.60 against 341.71). Fractal pivot lag: swing pivots require two bars on each side to confirm, so Thursday Nov 12's extremes are the newest pivots in the lists (NVDA's 148.80 low, AMD's 594.00 high, META's 618.92 low, AVGO's 369.82 high, SPCX's 147.60 high, SPY's 763.04 high); Friday's, Monday's and Tuesday's levels are in no list yet and those sessions' highs and lows are quoted from the bars. "Lowest close since", "first close under … since", "straight closes" and "after N closes over it" claims were checked against the daily bars with the 10-, 21-, 50- and 200-day averages recomputed from them; every 200-day figure quoted is the scan's. SPY's 732.44 is its first close under its 200-day since Nov 5 after seven closes over it and the lowest since Jul 29; MSFT's 506.24 is its first close under its 50-day since Nov 2 after ten closes over it and the lowest since Sep 24; AVGO is back over its 10-day and 21-day after one close under them and SPCX over its 10-day after two; HOOD's 69.19 matches its Apr 10 close; ORCL's 115.00 is the lowest since Jul 24, SNDK's 797.24 since Apr 8, IONQ's 24.84 since Apr 21, IGV's 95.74 since Jul 31; IONQ (24.07) and SKHY (117.40) printed new 52-week lows. The loaded history is 500 daily bars from Nov 2024; the 52-week high and low are the trailing 252 bars. SKHY's and SPCX's daily EMA50 are the scan's values on their short histories. The Nvidia and Fed headlines are on the feed only: no price, percentage or pre-market print from them appears in any number on this page.

Scorecard method. Tuesday's eight calls were graded on Tuesday's hourly bars (09:30 to 15:30 ET, seven bars) with the daily close as the final print. A long is on at the close of the first hour that closes over its reclaim while the hold has not been lost (AAPL and AMZN in the first hour); an open over the reclaim with the first target still above it is bought only when the second hour holds the reclaim (AVGO at the 10:30 close; TSLA's first hour closed 5 cents under its reclaim and the second hour under it, so nothing set up); an open over the first target is not an entry (AMD's long). A short is on at the close of the first hour that closes under its line (MSFT, NVDA in the first hour; AMD and META in the 10:30 hour after the first hour closed back inside the hold). A target printed before or inside the entry hour does not count for the entry; a trade whose remaining targets never print grades on the close against the entry, a wash inside a third of an ATR (NVDA 0.19 against, AAPL 0.27 against, AMD 0.24 against, META 0.08 against); a trade that prints a target after the entry hour works (MSFT's 507.12 and 504.96 in the 10:30 hour; AVGO's three targets in the 11:30 hour). A long is out at the first hourly close under its stop (AMZN at the 10:30 close, 0.38 ATR against, failed); a stop printed inside an hour that closes back over it does not stop the trade (AAPL's 10:30 hour, 5 cents through 350.43). A secondary trade on the same card is graded in the note and not in the tally (AMZN's short). Stance changes follow each card's own stated rule, one rung per close unless one bar crosses two rules, in which case the deeper rule applies; a rule written as "held a session" needs the second close (AVGO over 335.85, SPCX over 139.61, both pending today). Applied on Tuesday's close: nothing moved; MSFT lost its 50-day but its rule keeps the card cautious above 504.96. The levels quoted in the cards are the scan's Tuesday values.
